_doc: Small keys and boss keys (settings small_keys and boss_keys). Only loaded when one of them is not vanilla: with vanilla keys the key chests stay out of the world and the logic ignores keys (as before).

Per dungeon: game = DungeonInfo.<game> (GameData counter SmallKeyNum, flag IsGetBossKey) and the Banc folder; regions = logic regions of the dungeon (Ganon's Castle is an overworld region); region = region of the key chests; rule = prudent rule of every key chest (everything the dungeon may need, as the boss rules); small = small key chests (hash, room = DefaultDungeonRoomIndex in the map); freestanding = small keys lying on the ground (Obj_Dungeon_SmallKey: they stay with own_dungeon and removed, and are removed from the map with any_dungeon and random, their keys going to the item pool); boss_key = boss key chest; boss = locations behind the boss door; boss_events = events behind it.

Rule of one key chest: optional "rule" in its small / boss_key entry (default: the dungeon's rule). Without its key terms it must ask nothing more than the dungeon's rule (with own_dungeon the key chests are the key spots); a key count in it is used with any_dungeon and random.

Key counts: any location, event or exit rule may ask for keys itself, e.g. has(Small_Key_Forest_Temple, 2) or Boss_Key_Forest_Temple. With shuffled keys this replaces the prudent 'all the dungeon's small keys' (or the boss key) of its location; with vanilla or removed keys, and in the native generator, the term is always true.

layout: true once every rule of the dungeon that needs small keys says how many, in the worst case (the player may have opened other doors first): a rule without a key count then needs no key, nothing prudent is added, and small_keys=own_dungeon places the dungeon's keys anywhere in it by the logic. Without it (default) the logic stays prudent and own_dungeon keeps each key in a chest of its vanilla room.

name (optional, in a small / boss_key entry): the location name of that key chest, as shown in the plandomizer, the spoiler log and plando files; without it: <Dungeon> Small Key Chest <n> (n = rank in the list, not the order in the dungeon) or <Dungeon> Boss Key Chest. Names must be unique; a plando file using the old name must be updated.

start_keys: small keys owned from the start (GameData counter set at the new game, whatever the key settings; removed adds them to the full counter). Rule counts are the game's keys: has(Small_Key_<Dungeon>, n) asks for n - start_keys keys of the item pool (none: true).

unlocked_doors: chain-locked doors unlocked from the start, whatever the key settings: flag = the door's saved Bool (unnamed, #hash, found with tools.checkwatch while opening the door), set to true at the new game so the door loads as already unlocked; door = its map hash. Such a door is open in key_graph.json and needs no key. Fire Temple: the hammer-blocked door of the first room (room 0 -> 15), whose 8th key chest (room 22) is a normal location.
rooms: room of the other chests of these dungeons (own_dungeon: a small key may move to a chest of the same room, see World._key_spots).
Hashes and rooms read in the maps (tools.inventory, Banc/<game>/*.bcett.byml.zs); rules are prudent, not checked in game.
